events.excerpt: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google and Mozilla . Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969. November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device. This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes. According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploit
events.headline: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities

The money covers years of operating costs and has nothing to do with token reserves. The venture still has no CEO, no final name and no disclosed blockchain. A rival group of European banks already holds a license for its own euro stablecoin. A group of 21 banks and asset managers, including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Banco Santander and Deutsche Bank, has committed roughly $270 million to the company that will issue its planned U.S. dollar stablecoin, according to people familiar with the discussions. The commitments, reported on November 10, are meant to fund about five years of operations for the venture, known internally as Project Faro, which targets a launch in the first half of 2027 and would compete with Tether and Circle for institutional dollar payments. The $270 million pays for the issuer itself, meaning staff, technology, compliance and licensing, while the reserves backing each token will come later from the clients who buy them. The reporting does not show how much each institution contributed or whether all 21 members are paying in. A spokesperson for the project declined to comment, Goldman Sachs and Citi referred questions to the consortium,

events.excerpt: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations. These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns. To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models. Microsoft is also developing additional defenses, including AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools for detecting anomalous model modifications, and cryptographic model signing with tamper-evident provenance and audit trails. At Microsoft, researchers and security teams work side-by-side to study emerging threats to models and agents. Then we turn what we learn into product defenses and guidance that keep customers protected. More broadly, Lazarus is an example
events.headline: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents

events.excerpt: This proposal specifies the JSON document that tokenURI returns in ERC-721 and ERC-6909 and that uri returns in ERC-1155 . Most deployed tokens already use this format, but only part of it was ever specified. ERC-721 and ERC-1155 define name , description and image . Everything else wallets and marketplaces show ( animation_url , attributes and its display_type values, external_url , background_color ) comes from a page OpenSea published in 2018. Clients fill the gaps differently, so the same token renders differently from one app to the next. The URI schemes clients must resolve ( https , ipfs , ar , data ), the ones they may resolve ( ipns , and web3 from ERC-4804 ), and the ones they must never resolve. Fetching rules: ipfs:// URIs instead of gateway URLs, sandboxing HTML in animation_url , and keeping server-side fetches away from private addresses. events.excerpt: We recommend that all atlantic-2 validators and node operators update to v6.8.0-rc3 . The update is required for RPC nodes. There is no governance proposal and no coordinated chain halt. v6.8.0-rc3 is a release candidate on top of v6.8.0-rc2 . It makes wide eth_getLogs queries cheaper for RPC nodes and stops them early when the client cancels ( #4744 , #4790 , #4791 , #4799 , #4802 ). It also includes the v6.7.4 trace fix, so debug_trace* loads a past block's full validator set ( #4811 ). Wide log queries (over 100 blocks) share a node-wide limit of 30 queries per second. You can now change it with large_log_query_rps under [evm] in app.toml . Set it to 0 to turn the limit off. If the key is missing, the limit stays at 30 ( #4800 ). How to Update Build v6.8.0-rc3 with git fetch --tags && git checkout v6.8.0-rc3 && make install . Stop the node. Replace the seid binary with v6.8.0-rc3 . If you use Cosmovisor, replace the binary in upgrades/v6.8/bin/ . Start the node. Make sure that seid version shows v6.8.0-rc3 and that the node syncs new blocks. events.excerpt: Hi all — EnsRationis from Robonomics. Sensors.social is an open environmental data network I designed, and it is now growing across the EU. Everything is open source: the Altruist sensors that feed it, the software that collects the readings, and the map. Web3 does one job here, the one it is good at: it settles the data as a common good anyone can check, not a vendor’s database. How it works on Robonomics Owners who choose to share their Altruist’s data join the network; each sensor has its own key and signs every measurement it sends. A connectivity node checks the signature and that the sensor has an active subscription on Robonomics, a parachain on Polkadot, then passes the reading to the live map. The node collects readings into batches, stores each batch on IPFS and writes its hash to Robonomics. Anyone can fetch a batch and check it against the chain. The network is federated: a city or a lab can run its own connectivity node, and its sensors still show up on the common map. Next, with Robonomics 5.0: the reading the sensor signed goes on chain itself, so there is no need to trust the node at all. Try the map: https://sensors.social Happy to hear from anyone who wants to run a sensor in their city or build on the data. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
events.headline: Sensors.social: an open air-quality network on Polkadot is growing across the EU

events.excerpt: Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when recursively cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches. The fixes are included in Git 2.56.1 , with backports to Git 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git. Vulnerabilities in Git CVE-2026-111760: Code execution during recursive clones Git checks paths before writing files into a working tree, including rejecting paths that would overwrite its own repository metadata. However, an integer truncation in Git’s index handling can cause an extremely long path to pass validation under one name and then be written using a shorter name. An attacker can use this discrepancy to replace a submodule’s .git file with a symbolic link pointing to a directory containing malicious configuration or hooks . When Git subsequently uses that directory, it can execute attacker-controlled code during a recursive clone. The fix rejects extremely long index entry paths before their lengths can be truncated. [ Advisory ] CVE-2026-113408: Path traversal
events.headline: Git security vulnerabilities announced

events.excerpt: We propose an institution-managed user payment ledger for recording account debits and credits, enforcing spending capacity, and sealing account periods independently of funds settlement. Specification Draft PR #2159 Problem and scope A payment institution needs to distinguish a customer’s business entries from changes to the spending capacity it grants. It also needs to connect individual entries, current-period totals, and sealed periods when reconciling customer funds. An institution-level aggregate does not provide those per-account records. This proposal defines a common contract interface for those records and controls. It can serve an institution’s own business independently or compose with an on-chain payment protocol. It does not issue or transfer assets, establish customer identity, or prove that funds have been frozen or settled. Account model and interface Each account is scoped by (account, institution) . An institution can serve payer accounts, merchant accounts, or both; the same address at two institutions does not share records or capacity. Holding the account’s private key does not grant permission to write entries. events.excerpt: From snapshots to streams A sensor-facing agent may need to respond not just to the latest reading, but to an event that began many windows earlier, a running count, or a rule that changed while data kept arriving. That is the problem behind TimeOmni-Live, a model evaluated using LiveTS-Suite, a benchmark for Continuous & Live Time Series Understanding. The full paper describes a shift from one-shot analysis of fixed inputs toward maintaining state over an open-ended stream. The associated arXiv record identifies the same version, dated Nov. 6, 2026. Unlike a fixed-window model that receives a bounded sequence and stops, a continuous system must decide whether to respond as chunks arrive, preserve useful history, and incorporate queries or revised instructions during the stream. The benchmark tests those demands through tasks built around continuing streams and evolving instructions. What the benchmark asks LiveTS-Suite contains 5,249 streams, 15,555 annotated response events and 2.2 billion timesteps, organized into 18 tasks across six capability groups. The sequence begins with instantaneous conditions, such as recognizing a threshold, and sequential conditions that require multiple observations. It then moves to event tracking, where counts or event order matter, and event ref
events.headline: TimeOmni-Live tests the limits of memory in continuous sensor streams

events.excerpt: The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible. Yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize. Today’s materials challenges are different from those of the 20th century, but why are critical metals still produced using largely the same scientific foundations? events.excerpt: Benchmark contrast and calibration Researchers at Amazon recently detailed a method for optimizing Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, termed Higher-Order Pruning of Experts (HOPE). While the underlying research was detailed in an arXiv v3 paper dated Sept. 29, 2026, the team published a first-party Hugging Face article on Nov. 9, 2026, providing further context on the approach. In experiments using the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model at a 50% pruning rate, the researchers observed a performance contrast based on the calibration data employed. The study utilized two distinct domains: Evol-CodeAlpaca-v1, which is a coding-focused calibration dataset, and SWE-Bench Verified, which serves as an agentic trajectory calibration dataset. When calibrated with Evol-CodeAlpaca, the model achieved a score of 42.33 ±1.23 on the SWE-Bench Pro benchmark. When calibrated using SWE-Bench Verified trajectories, the score was 40.78 ±0.86. For comparison, the unpruned baseline for this model was 41.82. These figures represent scores multiplied by 100, derived as means and standard deviations from three independent calibration trials. In this tested case, one calibration set produced a mean above the baseline, while the other produced a mean below it. Mechanism: From first-order to HOPE Calibration is the proces

events.excerpt: The prdoc for the XCMv3 removal ( pr_13629.prdoc ) has a line the announcement here doesn’t have: “Assets trapped under a v3 hash become unclaimable.” I wanted to know how much that is on Polkadot, so I pulled every AssetsTrapped event for the relay and Asset Hub from Statescan and checked each hash against AssetTraps storage today. On the relay, 299 trap entries from the v3 period are still unclaimed, with 673.7 DOT in them. On Asset Hub there are 177, with 263.2 DOT and a bit of USDT and USDC. On both chains the v3 period runs from June 2023 to April 2024, when the runtimes moved to v4. Most of it belongs to ordinary accounts, not parachains. That’s 636.9 DOT across 224 accounts on the relay and 262.6 DOT across 116 accounts on Asset Hub. How it got there All but one of those account traps came from limitedTeleportAssets between the relay and Asset Hub. On the relay, most of the ones I opened show KilledAccount , then AssetsTrapped , then Attempted failing with FailedToTransactAsset . The account sent its whole balance, got reaped in the same transaction, and what the program had withdrawn went into the trap. On Asset Hub they fail with the same error, but the accounts weren’t reaped and most still hold DOT. A wallet team asked about these here in May 2024, and the answer then

events.excerpt: Goose has integrated a new mechanism for handling Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, targeting how their schemas are presented to the model. The implementation, detailed in Goose PR #13378 , adds a deferred loading strategy. This story concerns the merged Goose code change; it does not establish a separate tagged product release or a change to the MCP protocol itself. By default, Goose keeps its existing eager behavior, where tool schemas are provided to the model. Deferral is opt-in. When GOOSE_TOOL_DEFERRAL=lookup is set, Goose lists available MCP tool names in the system prompt rather than providing their schemas immediately. The model can call enable_tools with exact tool names; the selected schemas become available on the next response. The merged implementation validates those names against model-visible MCP tools. If any requested name is unknown or app-only, the enable request fails as a whole. Lookup is the only implemented strategy; the PR does not add search or wildcard matching. For builders, this creates an explicit selection step between seeing a tool’s name and seeing its schema. That can matter when designing an agent workflow: a tool not enabled is not among the schemas the model can use for its next response. But this is a change in schema availability, not a n
events.headline: Goose Implements Deferred MCP Tool Schema Loading
